graphEvents.label: What does embedding a second skill require

label: A Product Owner skill is a leaf package with a fixed part list: SKILL.md, graph-metadata.json, leaf-manifest.json, leaf-manifest.config.json, leaf-aliases.json, references/, assets/, changelog/, manual-testing-playbook/ and README.md.

The leaf manifest is generated by generate-leaf-manifest.cjs and leaf-aliases.json is its derived projection, regenerated through ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs --fix, so an embedded skill needs the generator in its loop.

graph-metadata.json declares skill identity and inter-skill edges (depends_on, enhances, siblings, conflicts_with, prerequisite_for) plus domains and intent signals, so a new skill must declare its position relative to sk-product-owner.
Product Owner is its own git repository nested in the workspace, which is the concrete form of the two-repository problem in the topic.
The package is explicitly a standalone single-mode skill with no mode-registry.json, so a parent-hub conversion is a structural change rather than a config toggle.

Adding a second skill touches four surfaces at once: a new skill directory, the AGENTS.md routing line that names only sk-product-owner today, the generated manifests, and the Project-side documentation.
